verdict: READY TO MERGE - 10 of 10 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Every test calls the real function under test with real inputs or tmp_path files and no mock chains; the ci.yml drift tests run against the real workflow file.
The DRIFTS parametrization first asserts the old text exists in ci.yml, so a reworded workflow fails the test loudly instead of passing as a no-op mutation.
The module loads by path with a sys.modules entry and cleanup, matching the neighboring tests/scripts files, and the one OS-dependent test carries cross_os plus a win32 skipif.
workflow_drift fails closed on the replay's command copies and exits 3 before any step runs, with an --ignore-drift escape.
Step semantics follow ci.yml closely: exit 5 read as a pass on Windows, the catalog runs after a failed pytest, and the hpy step is skipped after an earlier failure (matching the implicit success()).
fresh_out_dir refuses to empty a folder that lacks the tool's marker file, so a mistyped --out-dir cannot delete unrelated files.
Base-ref resolution is checked up front, so select_tests.py's silent fall back to a full run cannot masquerade as a selected run.
Functions are short, typed with Optional/Union-free typing, and the environment shaping is pure (ci_env, with_temp, dirty_warnings, shown take arguments) so it is testable without a Windows host.

CLAUDE.md:95-99 matches tools/ci_local.py: the --full, --python and --short-temp flags exist, exit 3 means drift or precondition, and the replay covers select_tests, -m cross_os pytest, the runtime catalog and the hpy check.
CLAUDE.md:73 now says the strict validation and mod tests run on Ubuntu only, which matches the plugins job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (runs-on ubuntu-latest).
tests/scripts/test_ci_local.py exists, so the drift-guard pointer in CLAUDE.md:99 is not dangling.
Every drift check is tested with a targeted ci.yml mutation (DRIFTS), so the guard is shown to fire for each check and not just to pass on the current file.
The replay reads select_tests.py's results through a real GITHUB_OUTPUT file, so it consumes the same output CI consumes instead of a parallel parse.
The comment at line 430 spells out GitHub's implicit success() rule for the hpy step, and run_windows encodes it: a catalog failure skips the hpy check, as it does on the runner.
fresh_out_dir only empties a folder that carries the tool's own marker file, so a mistyped --out-dir cannot wipe someone's work.
run_step resolves argv[0] against the replay PATH, which handles Windows' habit of searching the parent process's PATH.
The gap table says plainly what the replay cannot reproduce (merge commit, patch level, symlink privilege, code page) instead of overstating how faithful it is.
The CLAUDE.md edit is accurate: the plugins job does run on ubuntu-latest only, and the new paragraph matches the tool's flags and exit codes.

important.name: git_bash_dirs finds no Git Bash folder on the windows-latest runner
important.summary: CI run 43934925246 (pytest + ruff, windows-latest): tests/scripts/test_ci_local.py::test_git_bash_dirs_hold_sh fails with 'assert False' at test_ci_local.py:137; git_bash_dirs() returned no folder holding sh.exe. The step ran under C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.EXE. git_bash_dirs derives the Git root from shutil.which('git') by two .parent hops plus a mingw64 check (ci_local.py:170-174), so a git found outside the Git for Windows tree, or in a layout those hops miss, yields an empty list. Locally the function finds both folders whether PATH resolves git to Git/cmd, Git/bin or Git/mingw64/bin, so the failure cannot be reproduced here; the pasted CI output is the evidence. With an empty list the replay also loses Git Bash at the front of PATH (ci_env).
fix: Locate the Git root by walking up from shutil.which('git'), shutil.which('bash') and shutil.which('sh'), plus %ProgramFiles%/Git, to the first ancestor holding usr/bin/sh.exe; return its mingw64/bin and usr/bin. Give the test assert a message naming shutil.which('git') so a future CI failure shows the resolved path.

important.name: Isolated gitconfig writes safe.directory values unescaped
important.summary: isolated_git_global formats each entry as a raw `directory = <value>` line. `git config --get-all` prints the decoded value, so an entry stored as `E:\\work\\repo` comes back as `E:\work\repo` and gets written back with single backslashes. Git's config parser rejects unknown escapes like `\w` or `\a` with a fatal 'bad config line', and an unquoted `#` or `;` in a path starts a comment. With GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing at that file, every git call in the replay fails. select_tests.py catches the CalledProcessError and quietly falls back to a full plan ('diff unreadable, running everything'), which is the outcome preconditions() exists to prevent. preconditions() misses it because git_out runs in the caller's environment. Every git-using test then fails as well. The one function that writes a config file is also the one without a test.
fix: Build the file through git itself: create it empty, then run `git config --file <path> --add safe.directory <value>` once per entry, so git does its own escaping; add a test that round-trips an entry containing a backslash and a `#`.

Escape `\\` and `"` in each value and wrap it in double quotes (`directory = "..."`), then validate the result with `git config --file <path> --list` and report a precondition problem if git rejects it.

minor.name: fresh_out_dir deletion guard has no test
minor.summary:
tools/ci_local.py fresh_out_dir (lines 439-446) rmtrees a user-supplied --out-dir unless it holds files without the .ci-local marker. It is the one destructive operation in the tool, and no test covers either branch: refusing a non-empty unmarked folder, or emptying a marked one and rewriting the marker. A regression in the guard would delete a developer's folder silently.

Also (roast): fresh_out_dir is the only thing that stops a mistaken --out-dir from being rmtree'd, and run_windows holds the logic that mirrors CI's skip and fail order (both-none passes, pytest-none skips the hpy step, a pytest or catalog failure skips hpy, pip failure stops the run). Neither has a test. The tested helpers are the easy ones; the logic that can delete a folder or misreport a verdict is not.
fix: Add two tmp_path tests: an unmarked non-empty folder returns the 'holds files this tool did not write' message and keeps its files; a folder holding .ci-local is emptied and recreated with the marker; an empty or missing folder passes.
Add a test that fresh_out_dir refuses a non-empty folder without the marker and leaves its files in place, and that it clears a folder that has the marker.
Test run_windows with a tmp out_dir and a real tiny Selection (dry_run=True, or a stub python that exits with a chosen code) to cover the both-none, pytest-none and pytest-failure branches.

minor.name: Drift table covers one of several guarded lines per check
minor.summary:
workflow_drift checks SELECT_LINES (two lines: the --base form and the --full form) and PYTEST_LINES (three lines: the args assignment, the pytest command with the junit path, and the rc 5 test). DRIFTS mutates only the --base select line and the args=(-m cross_os) line. Changing the --full form, the --junitxml path or the rc = 5 comparison in ci.yml would be caught only by code the tests never exercise, so an accidental all()-to-any() edit passes. The hpy and pip cases are covered; the three missing mutations are cheap to add.

Also (tests): windows_rc, pytest_argv and skip_reasons are tested as pure helpers, but run_windows, run_tests and verdict carry the replay's behavior: skip the hpy step after an earlier failure, return a pass when selection is 'none', stop on a pip failure, add the catalog step to failed. None is exercised. Since run_step takes dry_run, a dry-run call with a hand-built Selection and Context is a behavioral test with no stubbing.
fix: Add DRIFTS rows for 'python tools/select_tests.py --full', '--junitxml=.artifacts/pytest-junit.xml' and '"$rc" = 5', each expecting its check name.
Add a test calling run_windows with dry_run=True, a Selection(pytest='none', ruff='none', ...) and a Selection with tests, asserting exit 0 and the printed step names via capsys.

minor.name: ci_env scrub test skips the RUNNER_ and CONDA_ prefixes
minor.summary: test_ci_env_drops_session_variables_and_marks_the_runner drops CLAUDE, HARNESS_, GIT_, PYTHON, GITHUB_ and VIRTUAL_ENV, but not RUNNER_* or CONDA_*, which SCRUB (tools/ci_local.py:75) also lists. It also asserts no non-scrubbed variable besides TEMP survives, and not MSYSTEM. Separately, the module docstring at tools/ci_local.py:16-17 lists the dropped variables without GITHUB_ and RUNNER_, which the code drops too.
fix: Add RUNNER_TEMP and CONDA_PREFIX to base and to the 'gone' tuple, and an unrelated variable such as APPDATA that must survive.
Add GITHUB_* and RUNNER_* to the docstring's list of dropped variables.

minor.name: Module and prepare docstrings do not match the environment and return contract in code
minor.summary:
The module docstring lists the dropped session variables as CLAUDE*, HARNESS_*, GIT_*, PYTHON*, CONDA_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, but SCRUB also drops GITHUB_* and RUNNER_*, and ci_env also sets MSYSTEM=MINGW64 and PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, which are not named although they change the environment seen by tests. prepare's docstring says 'notes ride along either way', but on the out-dir failure path the list is the problem and no notes are returned (main prints it without a 'problem:' prefix).

Also (roast): SCRUB drops CLAUDE*, HARNESS_*, GIT_*, PYTHON*, GITHUB_*, RUNNER_*, VIRTUAL_ENV and CONDA_*, but not PYTEST_ADDOPTS, PYTEST_PLUGINS or PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD. A developer's `-x`, `-p no:cacheprovider` or `-n auto` therefore rides into a replay that claims to match the runner. The module docstring's list of scrubbed prefixes also leaves out GITHUB_* and RUNNER_*, which the code does drop.
fix: Add GITHUB_*, RUNNER_*, MSYSTEM and PYTHONNOUSERSITE to the module docstring's environment paragraph.
Reword prepare's docstring: 'the context and the warning notes, or None and the problems'.
Add "PYTEST_" to SCRUB, list it in the docstring together with GITHUB_* and RUNNER_*, and add PYTEST_ADDOPTS to the `base` dict in test_ci_env_drops_session_variables_and_marks_the_runner.

minor.name: workflow_drift raises instead of reporting drift when the python job is renamed or removed
minor.summary:
The module docstring promises that workflow_drift exits 3 on a mismatch. job_lines uses lines.index(f"  {job}:"), which raises ValueError when ci.yml no longer has a `python:` job. main calls workflow_drift without a guard, so the user gets a traceback (exit 1) in place of the 'ci.yml no longer matches this replay' message. Renaming a job is a drift case this guard exists for.

Also (runtime): workflow_drift compares the commands, the step order, the matrix and the setup-python version. run_windows also copies ci.yml's `if:` logic: pip install runs when pytest or ruff is not 'none', pytest, hpy and the catalog follow `pytest != 'none'`, the catalog is `!cancelled()` plus the JUnit file, and hpy gets an implicit success() (comment at line 430). JOB_TIMEOUT_S mirrors `timeout-minutes: 15`. None of these is compared, so editing a condition in ci.yml leaves the replay quietly out of date, which the module docstring says drift detection prevents.

Also (roast): workflow_drift compares commands, step order, the matrix, the Python version and the ruff `if:`, but none of the other `if:` expressions that run_windows reimplements by hand: the pip step's `pytest != 'none' || ruff != 'none'`, pytest's `pytest != 'none'`, the catalog's `!cancelled() && hashFiles(...)`, and the hpy step's condition with no status function (the comment at line 430 depends on it). Changing any of them, for example hpy to `always()`, keeps the drift guard green while the replay's gating no longer matches CI. A drift guard that skips the branch logic only guards half of the replay.

Also (roast): job_lines calls `lines.index(f"  {job}:")`, which raises ValueError when the `python` job is renamed or removed. main() then exits with a traceback instead of the documented exit 3 and its 'ci.yml no longer matches' message, and test_replay_matches_the_workflow errors instead of failing on a named check. Renaming the job is exactly the kind of change this check is supposed to catch.
fix: In job_lines, return [] when the job header is absent (or catch ValueError in workflow_drift) so the 'python job step order' check fails and main exits 3 with the drift message.
Add checks that the `if` text of the pip, pytest and hpy steps and of the catalog step equals a copied constant, and that `timeout-minutes: 15` appears in the job lines.
State in the module docstring that only the commands, order and matrix are guarded and that conditions are not.
Add one check per condition to `checks` (exact `steps.get(<label>, blank).cond == "..."` comparisons for the pip line, pytest, CATALOG_STEP and HPY_STEP), plus a DRIFTS row in the test for each one.
In workflow_drift, return ["python job present"] when `"  python:"` is not among the workflow lines, before calling job_lines; add a DRIFTS row that renames the job.

minor.name: core.autocrlf row reports the caller's global config, not the replay's
minor.summary:
The replay swaps the global git config for an isolated file (isolated_git_global, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL in ci_env). gap_rows reads core.autocrlf through git_out, which runs in the caller's real environment, so the 'local' column shows the caller's global value while the replayed pytest sees only repo-local and system config. The table is meant to show the replay's difference from CI, and here it can show a value the replay never uses.

Also (roast): If the target interpreter cannot be launched, python_facts reports version 'unrunnable'. version_problem accepts that version whenever --any-python is set, so preconditions pass, and run_select's subprocess.run on a missing executable raises FileNotFoundError: the user gets a traceback where exit 3 with a problem line was expected. The flag is meant to waive the 3.11 requirement, not the requirement that the interpreter works.
fix: Give git_out an optional env argument and pass ctx.env for the core.autocrlf and git --version rows, so the row shows what the replay sees.
In preconditions, report `--python <path> does not run` whenever ctx.facts["version"] == "unrunnable", whether or not --any-python is set; extend test_version_gate_accepts_only_311 to cover it.

minor.name: dry-run never prints the catalog command
minor.summary:
The --dry-run help says it will 'select, then print the other commands'. run_tests guards the catalog step with junit.is_file(), and a dry run never writes the JUnit file, so the catalog command is skipped silently. The pip, pytest and hpy commands do print. The dry run therefore shows 3 of the 4 later commands, and the catalog step is the one whose argv (junit and output paths) is least obvious.

Also (runtime): parse_args applies Path.absolute() to --python, so a bare name such as `--python python` becomes <cwd>/python, which does not exist. python_facts swallows the OSError and returns version 'unrunnable', and version_problem then reports 'python unrunnable is not 3.11.x', which hides the real cause. With --any-python the problem is skipped, and run_select then raises FileNotFoundError from subprocess.run (traceback, not exit 3). The docstring documents `--python EXE` and exit 3 for preconditions.
fix: In run_tests, enter the catalog branch when `junit.is_file() or args.dry_run`, and call print_skips only when the file exists, so run_step prints the catalog command and returns 0 on a dry run.
Narrow the --dry-run help and docstring wording to say the catalog step is shown only after a real pytest run.
In parse_args, resolve a name with no directory part through shutil.which before .absolute().
In preconditions, add an explicit problem when facts['version'] == 'unrunnable' (e.g. 'cannot run <python>'), independent of --any-python, so exit 3 is returned before the select step.

minor.name: skip_reasons lets a malformed JUnit file crash the run after pytest has already reported
minor.summary: run_tests parses the JUnit file with ElementTree.parse and catches nothing. A report truncated by a killed pytest (timeout) or a crash raises ParseError, so the user gets a traceback instead of the verdict line, and the catalog step and the exit code 1 are lost.
fix: Wrap the parse in try/except ElementTree.ParseError and return an empty dict (optionally print 'junit unreadable'), so run_tests continues to the catalog step and the verdict.
